title: Chargeback Spike
premise: Marketplace Lumen, 6-12 October 2026: chargebacks tripled in a week and the risk team is paged. Eight systems saw parts of it, several of them dirty, and none agree on what anything is called. What explains it?

sources.name: Order Ledger
sources.blurb: The storefront's order export. Comma CSV with quoted names; seller names as the storefront spelled them that day. Some timestamps are in US format and a few buyer ids are blank.

sources.name: Payment Gateway
sources.blurb: One JSON object per authorization attempt. Epoch milliseconds, except where someone logged seconds. One line is not even JSON.

sources.name: Device Fingerprints
sources.blurb: A fingerprinting collector's session dump: camelCase, three levels deep, and its clock runs an hour ahead.

sources.name: Help Desk
sources.blurb: Support tickets as XML. Reporters are emails, not account ids; a tenth have no opened date; the one change ticket matters.

sources.name: Dispute Export
sources.blurb: The card network's dispute file: a schema, then bare rows. Dates as dd/mm/yyyy, four of them 00/00/0000.

sources.name: Seller Registry
sources.blurb: Onboarding records with legal names and payout accounts. Two sellers share a payout account. A country of '-' and a rating of 'unknown'.

sources.name: Promo Catalog
sources.blurb: key=value lines. No per-record dates: the whole export is dated by its header.

sources.name: Partner Fraud Feed
sources.blurb: Indicators from a fraud-intel partner: card BINs, device fingerprints, merchant names and emails, each with its own confidence. Names are free text; three indicators have no date.
